title: The Emptied Room
logline: An elderly woman gives away what is left of a house she has lived in for sixty years, and Chathura leaves her doorway for a road that, by evening, puts him down in the middle of a crowded city junction.

object.note: Object 10 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject. Object 1, the first object, may also be carried into the day that ends in the crowd.

thread_in.thread: Stepping away without abandoning anyone leads to a final giving away: an elderly woman emptying a house of sixty years, and a doorway that becomes Chathura's road toward the crowd.

thread_out.thread: Ends on the crowded-location event → Episode 100 Part A.

release.pinned_note: last film in story time; ends on the crowd shared with Episodes 1 and 100

A road connecting that home to a real, busy Sri Lankan city junction

lesson.in_simple_terms: The peace the texts point to at the end of the road is not something made or gained, and it is not a feeling or a place. They describe it as very near but covered over, and as the last of the four basic realities the series began with.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ගමනේ අවසානයේ ග්‍රන්ථ පෙන්වා දෙන නිවන සාදාගන්නා දෙයක්වත්, හැඟීමක්වත්, ස්ථානයක්වත් නොව, ඉතා ළඟින් ඇති නමුත් වැසී ඇති දෙයක් ලෙස දක්වා තිබේ.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma names four ultimate realities (paramattha dhamma): consciousness, mental factors, matter and, fourth and last, Nibbāna. Nibbāna is taught as unconditioned (asaṅkhata): not produced by any cause, without arising, ageing or passing away, without shape or location, and not a pleasant feeling, yet not an empty nothing. The texts say it is realised directly rather than manufactured, and the Margaya calls it very near, covered by the aggregates that ignorance and craving keep taking up again. They also say it lies beyond reasoning and has to be seen for oneself.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film watches an elderly woman sort what remains: things given away, kept or simply left, and her own account of what each meant and why it can now go. The room empties until only the last light through the window is left; the camera does not claim to show peace, only a life visibly ceasing to add to itself. Then Chathura leaves the doorway, and by evening the road has put him down in a crowded city junction of traffic and overlapping sound, the image that opens Episode 1.

key_terms.en: the unconditioned; the complete stilling of craving, the aggregates and suffering
ultimate realities (consciousness, mental factors, matter, nibbāna)

lesson.caution: The emptied room is not Nibbāna, and the film says nothing about the woman's inner state: the texts deny that this peace is a mood, a place or a nothingness, so any calm a camera can film is at most a pointer.
lesson.builds_on: The fishing family stepped away while keeping every obligation; this film follows a final giving away and turns from what people set down to what the texts say is uncovered, not built.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
